digest.intro: Infrastructure as battlefield, biology bending hard, and three cable-robot rabbit holes.

items.title: Data Centers Go Underground as Ukraine's Drones Hit Russian AI Compute
items.blurb: Ukraine has taken out facilities run by Yandex, Sberbank, VKontakte, and the Russian Ministry of Finance — forcing Rostelcom into talks with a nickel mining company about moving servers into tunnels, and one regional governor proposing open-pit coal mines with green parks planted above as camouflage. Putin simultaneously signed a decree requiring data center operators to reserve 10% of capacity for state emergency use. The concept of data sovereignty just acquired a literal geology.

items.title: North Korea Turned a Fake Job Interview Into the Largest Crypto Heist in History — $6.3B from Binance
items.blurb: A months-long DPRK state operation used fake HR processes and social engineering to infiltrate Binance's supply chain and walk off with $6.3 billion — not via a code exploit but through the oldest vector: a person who thought they were interviewing a candidate. It's the clearest demonstration yet that the most dangerous attack surface in any system is the hiring process.

sections.heading: Biology doing things it wasn't supposed to

items.title: GLP-1s Beat Metformin for Prediabetes — 31% Lower T2D Risk, Fewer Heart Events, Longer Survival
items.blurb: In 250,000+ adults with prediabetes and obesity, GLP-1 receptor agonists made participants 1.5× more likely to fully normalize blood sugar compared to metformin, with lower T2D progression, fewer heart attacks and strokes, and lower all-cause mortality over five years. This is the first large independent head-to-head comparison — not industry-funded — and it's already reshaping the prediabetes standard-of-care conversation. Still conference abstract, not yet peer-reviewed as a full manuscript.

items.title: Stringman: A $800 Cable-Driven Robot That Grips Across an Entire Room
items.blurb: Four motors, ceiling anchors, and a hanging gripper that covers any room up to 10m diagonal — with 1.9kg average payload versus 0.32kg for a comparable 7-actuator arm, because the load is shared across all lines simultaneously. At under $800 in materials with fully open-source 3D-printed parts, Stringman inverts the usual robotics cost model: instead of buying more actuators to reach further, you buy geometry. The clutter-immunity (it works from above, so floor chaos is irrelevant) is a legitimately useful design insight.

items.title: [VIDEO] Bambu H3C Toolchanger: 9 Independent Tools, Sub-6-Second Swaps
items.blurb: CNC Kitchen is the highest signal-to-noise channel for desktop fabrication, and the H3C is the most consequential hardware drop in the space in years: nine fully independent tool heads with material swaps under six seconds means multi-material printing stops being a party trick and starts being a real workflow. Worth watching for the hands-on stress tests alone.

items.title: Marian Wawrzeniecki's Neopagan Paintings: Archaeology as Myth, Myth as Political Act
items.blurb: A Polish painter-archaeologist who actually discovered the first obsidian artifacts on Polish soil used that fieldwork to construct an entirely parallel visual mythology — one designed to displace Christian iconography with a pre-Christian Slavic identity at a moment when Poland didn't legally exist as a country. The 1910 canvas described here, a skull-faced nude bisecting Art Nouveau tableaux with the title 'Old Truth Lies in Books,' sits at the uncomfortable intersection of serious scholarship and nationalist myth-fabrication. The Public Domain Review essay is one of those pieces that makes the word 'minor painter' feel like a category error.

facts.fact: A Russian regional governor has formally proposed building data centers inside open-pit coal mines with green public parks planted on top as camouflage from drone strikes.
Stringman achieves 1.9 kg average payload across a room using only 4 motors — a 7-actuator serial arm using the same motors manages just 0.32 kg.

The Nvidia RTX Spark laptop's GPU runs at ~780 MHz on Linux versus 2.2 GHz on Windows because the power management firmware is encrypted and only the Windows driver can decrypt it, cutting inference throughput from 65 to 14 tokens per second.
Roughly 2.8 million basketwork eels — 3,550 metric tons of biomass — gather annually at a single underwater mountain off Tasmania, and researchers still don't know exactly why.

The 2.8-million-year-old Taung child skull shows talon scratches around the eye sockets that match the characteristic marks left by African crowned eagles on monkey skulls — suggesting a large bird killed one of our earliest known hominin relatives.

make_something.prompt: Build a Stringman-style cable-position simulator in WebGL: four anchor points at ceiling corners, a hanging gripper, and real-time inverse kinematics as you drag the gripper through the volume. Visualize line tension as color — white at center where load is shared evenly, red near corners where one line takes the strain. Bonus: add a UI that lets you place obstacles on the floor and show the gripper navigating around them from above, the one thing wheeled robots can't do.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film-length meditation on memory, ritual, and how images construct reality — Marker moves between Tokyo game arcades, Guinea-Bissau ceremonies, and Icelandic volcanoes and finds the same invisible system underneath. It will make you want to shoot something immediately.

art_picks.title: Myron Stout — Works on Paper
art_picks.creator: Myron Stout
art_picks.why: One of the great obsessives: Stout would spend years on a single small painting, rotating between pure black and white, trying to hold the exact moment a form became figure. The patience required to get there is encoded in the surface — expressive minimalism at its strangest.

art_picks.title: Plagues
art_picks.creator: This Will Destroy You
art_picks.why: Post-rock built as systems — long arcs of building tension released in precise, devastating moments. No vocals to hide behind, so the structure has to carry everything; it does. The kind of record that resets the room.

events.name: Ólafur Arnalds
events.venue: The Town Hall, 123 W 43rd St, Manhattan
events.why: Arnalds builds neoclassical-electronic systems live — generative MIDI triggers, strings, and his own piano locked into feedback loops that change each night; it's the rare show where the architecture of the music is the spectacle.

events.name: Cristina Iglesias: Possible Matter
events.why: Iglesias debuts an immersive dome installation and wall-based sculptures probing where built infrastructure ends and natural world begins — exactly the physical/digital/material edge you live at.

events.name: Hard Art — MoMA PS1
events.why: A major survey of abstract painting by Black artists from 1969 to now, spanning three generations — the kind of institutional argument that redraws a lineage rather than just hanging paintings.

events.name: Collectible New York 2026
events.why: Design fair staged inside a decommissioned cinema — the building itself is part of the argument — spotlighting contemporary collectible objects at the craft/art/furniture blur, with a talks program that actually goes deep.

events.name: Art Week NYC — Gallery Openings & Walking Tours
events.venue: Chelsea, Tribeca/SoHo, LES, Upper East Side (citywide)
events.why: 80+ galleries doing coordinated evening openings and neighborhood walks — not a fair, so no booths, just studios and spaces moving in sync; a rare moment to cover a lot of ground in one focused burst.
